text:
maria: Hey team — we hit an IP/ENI bottleneck in ap-northeast-1 while bringing up the new GPU nodepools for the Dedicated fleet. Need quota bump and IPv6 prefix support.

alex: quick summary of what failed? logs / error we can show to AWS?

maria: kube events showed AttachNetworkInterface errors during scale-up: 
```
Warning  FailedAttachVolume  2m (x10 over 6m)  attachdetach-controller  AttachNetworkInterface failed for pod/gpu-pool-xyz: insufficient available addresses in subnet
```

jon: same cluster showed ENI exhaustion on a few instance-types, looks like we bumped into the per-instance ENI limit for the instance profile when we use multiple ENIs per GPU VM.

sam: we’re provisioning g5.12xlarge and g5.24xlarge — they need many secondary IPs for pod-managed IPs (AWS CNI IP per pod). subnet /24s were nearly full.

maria: ask to AWS: increase Elastic IPs for account in ap-northeast-1 by 250, increase ENI quota per instance type (or account-level ENIs) to support target capacity, and allocate an IPv6 prefix ( /56 ) for VPC prefix delegation so we can move to IPv6 pod IPs and reduce IPv4 headroom. Also we want Raise for VPCs per region from 5 -> 20.

alex: can you paste suggested language I can file with support? I’ll open the request and link infra ticket.

maria: sure — copy/paste below: 

"Hello AWS support, we are provisioning a Dedicated GPU fleet in ap-northeast-1 and require the following quota increases to avoid capacity bottlenecks during cluster scale-ups: 
1) Increase Elastic IPs (VPC) quota from current 50 to 300 for account X (usage: many public endpoints and nat gateway fallbacks for dedicated pools). 
2) Increase the maximum number of network interfaces per region/account to support 2000 ENIs (or increase per-instance ENI limits for g5 instances to allow 8 ENIs per instance). 
3) Increase VPCs per Region limit from 5 to 20 (we will host isolated VPCs per customer/dedicated pool). 
4) Allocate one IPv6 Prefix (/56) to allow prefix delegation for multiple subnets and reduce IPv4 address pressure.
We can provide usage graphs and scale plan on request. Please escalate to the networking quota team. Thank you."

alex: sending now. attaching cluster logs and a short cost impact note.

netops-bot: Support case created: case-20240328-985 (aws-support). Estimated initial response 24-48 hrs.

maria: FYI cost side — if AWS can't allocate IPv6 prefix we’ll need to keep larger contiguous IPv4 blocks which increases cross-AZ NAT bandwidth and potential NAT gateway cost. Ballpark: +$1.5k/mo per additional NAT GW for each subnet pair we carve out.

jon: action items: alex=own support case, sam=prepare subnet expansion plan and IPAM mapping, maria=prepare capacity forecast showing required ENIs and EIPs by week for next 12 weeks.

sam: for IPAM plan I’ll propose /21 and /22 allocations per AZ and a route to migrate existing staging pools first.

alex: update from AWS: "We've received your request and we need justification for Elastic IP increase and VPC limit increase. Please provide expected public IP usage and customers/VPC count."

maria: I’ll upload the usage matrix (public endpoints per pool, failover requirements). Also adding notes: we can accept staggered increase — EIPs first, then ENI/vpc limits.

aws-support: (automated) Please provide the number of public IPv4s in use today and the projected 90-day peak. Also include whether you can use Elastic Network Interfaces attached to NAT GW endpoints as alternative.

maria: current public IPv4s in use: 68. projected 90-day peak: 240. Will include that in the case.

jon: while this is pending we should add a temporary mitigation: 1) increase IP reuse by enabling prefix assignment for pods (when available), 2) scale node pools more slowly, 3) shift some canaries to IPv6-only endpoints in staging.

sam: noted — will schedule canary shifts for next Tuesday.

alex: marking case-20240328-985 as high-priority. I’ll post AWS reply here when we get it. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks. if anyone else sees AttachNetworkInterface spikes, drop logs here and we’ll add to the support case.
